Bournemouth Secure Carabao Cup Quarter‑Final Spot with 3‑0 Win Over Aston Villa; Sunderland Edge Brentford 3‑2 to Reach Last Eight

Carabao Cup Round‑of‑16 Results – A Double Header of Late‑Night Drama

The Carabao Cup fourth round delivered two contrasting stories on Tuesday night. At the Vitality Stadium, Bournemouth thrashed Aston Villa 3‑0 to book a place in the competition’s quarter‑finals for the first time in eight seasons, while at the Stadium of Light Sunderland produced a three‑goal burst in a ten‑minute spell to defeat Brentford 3‑2 and become the competition’s latest last‑eight entrant.

Bournemouth’s Clinical Performance

Marco Rose’s Cherries opened the scoring in the seventh minute through winger Amine Adli, who finished a fine team move after a lofted cross from full‑back Julio Soler. The goal set up a fifth consecutive win across all competitions for Bournemouth. The captain, Lewis Cook, doubled the lead early in the second half with a low, in‑swinger from a short corner, and Álvaro Rodríguez sealed the win in the 69th minute, converting a rebound after Tyler Adams intercepted a loose pass.

Villa, five‑time League Cup winners, struggled to create clear chances. Their unfamiliar lineup saw goalkeeper Marco Bizot make a crucial save to deny Ben Gannon‑Doak, and substitute Alysson missed a late header. Bournemouth’s defence kept a fifth clean sheet in a row, and the result means they will travel to Anfield to face Liverpool in the quarter‑finals.

Sunderland’s Late‑Night Surge

Régis Le Bris’s Sunderland started the match strongly, taking a 3‑0 lead by the 33rd minute. Chemsdine Talbi, Timur Tutierov and Malick Fofana were on target, with winger Jocelin Ta Bi involved in all three goals. The home side’s dominance was threatened when Callum Wilson pulled one back within three minutes, tapping in off the bar after a scuffed shot from Vitaly Janelt.

The match stretched into five minutes of added time after Igor Thiago’s header appeared to have crossed the line but was cleared by the goalkeeper Melker Ellborg. Despite a late scare when Thiago’s header slipped under Ellborg, Sunderland held on. The victory marks their first appearance in the last eight of the Carabao Cup in five years, a period when they were still a League One club.

Brentford’s Fight Ends in Disappointment

Brentford, who started strongly with a free header from captain Nathan Collins and a Michael Kayode effort that rattled the post, could not convert their early pressure into a goal. Mamadou Sangaré’s volley was tipped over the bar by Ellborg, and later attempts from Jannik Schuster and Dango Ouattara missed the target. The Bees’ hopes of a comeback were extinguished by Sunderland’s clinical finishing.

What Readers Can Verify

The official match reports and statistics are available on the Premier League’s website and the Carabao Cup’s official page. Detailed event timelines, player appearances and goal videos can be cross‑checked against the source article at [The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/28/carabao-cup-fouth-round-bournemouth-aston-villa-sunderland-brentford).

Practical Implications

  • Bournemouth – The win continues a positive run for the Cherries, who will now face Liverpool, a top‑four side, in the quarter‑finals. Their defensive solidity (five clean sheets) suggests they can pose a problem for any opponent, but they will need to improve their final third efficiency to compete against a side of Liverpool’s quality.
  • Sunderland – The victory marks a significant milestone for the club, highlighting their rapid progression from League One to challenging Premier League sides. Their ability to score quickly and defend resolutely will be key when they travel to Crystal Palace, another team looking to make a cup impact.
  • Fans & Fantasy Managers – Both matches featured multiple goal scorers and a high‑tempo attacking style, offering plenty of fantasy points. The quarter‑final draw will be made later this week, but the two new qualifiers (Bournemouth vs Liverpool and Sunderland vs Crystal Palace) are already set for the week commencing 14 December.
  • Verification – Readers can confirm the scores, goal scorers and line‑ups by checking the match pages on the official Premier League and Carabao Cup websites, as well as the published article linked above.

The Carabao Cup continues to deliver unexpected storylines, with Bournemouth and Sunderland both securing historic progression into the competition’s knockout phase.
